items.title: Hijacked email accounts complicate investigations into European bomb hoaxes
items.summary: Bomb threats sent to thousands of schools across Europe originated from a compromised email account at a Taiwanese university, following a pattern of hoax threats targeting airports and newsrooms via legitimate institutions.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach
items.summary: Apify detected unauthorized access to internal systems, rotated critical secrets, revoked some third‑party OAuth connections, and required users to reset 2FA.

items.title: Hacked Asian Telcos Used to Intercept Taiwanese Calls and Texts
items.summary: Enea linked SilentAir and Liminal Panda to attacks on Asian mobile operators that were used to intercept calls and texts in Taiwan.

items.title: Lego Takes BrickLink Marketplace Offline After Detecting Unusual Activity
items.summary: Lego shut down its BrickLink Marketplace following detection of unusual activity while investigating the incident.

items.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch Over 180 Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Google released Chrome 157 fixing 83 vulnerabilities, and Mozilla released Firefox 160 addressing 99 bugs, together patching over 180 security issues.

items.title: Attacker Targets 60,000 GitHub Repositories in Credential Theft Campaign
items.summary: The wfx-loot campaign deployed a CI secret stealer across more than 1,800 GitHub repositories, affecting up to 60,000 repositories through hijacked accounts.

items.title: Operation Endgame malware takedown turns up over 6 million stolen logins
items.summary: Police and Europol dismantled servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware, recovering over 6 million stolen credentials from infected computers.

items.title: Romania says it stopped Russian cyberattack targeting government emails
items.summary: Romania’s intelligence agency halted a Russian state‑linked cyber‑espionage campaign before the attackers could exfiltrate sensitive government email data.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations
items.summary: Daylight secured $80 million in funding to accelerate product development, hire talent, expand its U.S. presence, and enter new markets.

items.title: Hackers exploiting ScreenConnect plugin flaw to spread malware across hundreds of PCs
items.summary: ConnectWise disabled third‑party extensions in 400 environments after bughunters discovered an authentication flaw that could let attackers bypass MFA and spread malware via the ScreenConnect plugin.

items.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
items.summary: Suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers used an AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments, steal sensitive documents, and infiltrate critical infrastructure networks.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that Windows updates released since October 2026 Patch Tuesday are causing SQL Server performance and stability issues.

items.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
items.summary: Google Cloud warned that three side‑channel flaws in AMD Turin CPUs could allow a VM to read data from other processes or the kernel, and recommends guest OS patches and reboot.

items.title: Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones
items.summary: Penlink’s Webloc tool collects location data from weather, gaming, email, and religious apps on smartphones and sells the service to police, enabling detailed tracking over the past year.

items.title: Webinar: See How Identity Blind Spots Put Your SOC at Risk and How to Close Them
items.summary: The webinar discusses how identity blind spots can expose SOCs to risk, emphasizing the need to quickly identify actors behind suspicious activity and the potential for AI agents to misuse permissions.

items.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
items.summary: N‑able reported new vulnerabilities in N‑central 2026.4.1 HF2 that allow remote code execution and SYSTEM access when the Legacy API is exposed to the internet.

items.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
items.summary: Material Security identified a phishing campaign that hijacked live Google sessions via calendar invites and live proxies, and has taken down hundreds of attacker domains.

items.title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution
items.summary: PTC released patches for CVE‑2026‑126325, a critical flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM that could allow remote code execution through improper input validation and deserialization.

items.title: European tech buyers add digital sovereignty to cyber shopping list
items.summary: EU tech buyers are prioritizing digital sovereignty in procurement decisions, influenced by NIS2, DORA, and other regulatory factors.

items.title: Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack
items.summary: The Fireworks AI hack compromised chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces, with most transcripts unattributable.

items.title: Microsoft Entra adds a seven-day safeguard against irreversible identity deletion
items.summary: Microsoft Entra preview feature Hard Deletion Protection gives administrators a seven‑day window to recover selected identities before permanent deletion. It applies to cloud‑only users, groups, and applications.

items.title: Stolen Claude API keys can turn Claude Code into a remote-controlled implant
items.summary: Darktrace researchers showed that stolen Claude API keys can redirect Claude Code into a remote‑controlled implant, enabling exfiltration of large files via the Claude Files API.

items.title: Inside an AI Attack Against a US Retailer
items.summary: Attackers used AI‑generated scripts to achieve lateral movement within a US retailer’s network after hand‑typed commands failed, breaching the system in minutes.

items.title: Security Teams Must Shift from Patching to Mitigation in the AI Era
items.summary: Symantec’s Dick O’Brien argues that the shrinking patch window forces organizations to adopt an assume‑exploit mindset and focus on mitigation rather than patching.

items.title: Hackers Deploy Malware in Fresh ScreenConnect Campaign
items.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a legitimate ScreenConnect extension to bypass authentication and deploy malware, as reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that November 2026 security updates fail to install on Windows 11 systems running the October preview update, affecting update reliability.

items.title: Photos: IRISSCON 2026 cybercrime conference
items.summary: IRISSCON 2026, held at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium, showcased current cyber threats and practical response strategies, with industry partners such as Help Net Security in attendance.

items.title: Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works
items.summary: The article introduces a series on cloud penetration testing, covering external, overlay, and underlay layers, common architectures like OpenStack and Kubernetes, typical attack chains, and real‑world incidents.

items.title: NCSC Launches Cyber Adversary Testing to Boost Resilience
items.summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre launched a Cyber Adversary Simulation scheme to test and improve organizations’ cyber resilience.

items.title: Hackers Target N-central Zero-Days as N-able Rushes Patches
items.summary: After a researcher disclosed over 30 zero‑days, hackers targeted N‑central while N‑able released patches for unauthenticated vulnerabilities, as reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
items.summary: Threat actors use GSocket, a legitimate open‑source remote access tool, to maintain persistence on Linux servers even after initial vulnerabilities are patched. The tool is embedded to keep access.

items.title: AWS Emulator: Open-source tool for testing AWS apps locally, built by autonomous AI agents
items.summary: AWS released AWS Emulator, a free open‑source tool that simulates AWS services locally. It was written entirely by autonomous AI agents, with no engineer code, and incurs no extra service fee.

items.title: London hotel put admin login for booking website on whiteboard behind the front desk
items.summary: A London hotel displayed the admin login credentials for its booking website on a whiteboard behind the front desk, exposing them to anyone in the lobby.

items.title: Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover
items.summary: MongoDB Server has a pre‑authentication flaw (CVE‑2026‑118383) that lets attackers send two requests to crash the server. The crash occurs when the server later becomes primary during failover. Fixed versions were released.

items.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay allows attackers to steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and maintain persistent access. Red Hat has issued a patch.

items.title: Maersk Reveals Data Breach as Extortion Group Demands $5m
items.summary: Maersk announced that a threat actor extracted data from a legacy system and an extortion group demanded $5 million for the data.

items.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft Amid $5 Million Extortion Attempt
items.summary: Maersk confirmed that the WhiteArmor ransomware group stole 100 GB of data from its systems and that the group is demanding $5 million in ransom.

items.title: .NET 11 security changes target the software supply chain
items.summary: Microsoft released .NET 11, a Standard Term Support release that focuses on software supply‑chain integrity, authentication handling, and platform lifecycle. It includes updates to C# 15, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows development.

items.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data
items.summary: Node.js fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including two HTTP/2 bugs that could crash servers or leak memory contents to other connections. Updated versions are available for 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Autofix and the question of who owns a bad AI patch
items.summary: GitHub’s VP discussed accountability for AI‑generated patches that fix one flaw but introduce another, explaining how Agentic Autofix re‑runs detection engines and tests, and advising CISOs on metrics and codebase readiness.

items.title: Japan Pushes Emergency Funding for Cybersecurity as AI-Assisted Breaches Rise
items.summary: Japan pushes emergency funding for cybersecurity, adding public‑private responders, an AI‑focused team, and expanded use of active cyber‑defense powers.

items.title: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach at third-party provider
items.summary: Baker Tilly Advisory Group informs clients of a data breach that compromised personal information of clients and their dependents.

items.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
items.summary: Unit 42 reports on attacker use of AI‑powered red team tools (ARTEX) and offers mitigation guidance for defenders.

items.title: Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations
items.summary: ConnectWise investigates a malware campaign targeting MSPs via compromised ScreenConnect environments to deploy rogue remote‑access clients.

items.title: Attackers Say 'Hello' to a Different Scale of Cloud Attack
items.summary: Researchers identify a cloud attack chain dubbed "Greeter" where attackers leave "hello" messages in logs to obscure their trail.

items.title: eMudhra revokes 8 more CA certificates after private key mishap
items.summary: eMudhra revokes eight additional intermediate CA certificates after discovering improper private key handling during certificate generation.

items.title: AI Raises the Stakes for Cyber Resilience
items.summary: AI‑driven threats increase the importance of rapid business disruption recovery as a competitive advantage.

items.title: Notion says Fireworks breach exposed customer AI chat transcripts
items.summary: Notion disclosed that a breach at AI provider Fireworks AI exposed Notion AI chat transcripts in a limited number of workspaces.

items.title: N-able Takes N-central Platform Offline After Discovery of 33 Flaws
items.summary: N‑able takes its N‑central platform offline after finding 33 flaws, releasing a hotfix to mitigate public exploits.

items.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
items.summary: Investigation points to a 36‑year‑old man in St. Petersburg as the administrator of ransomware group Qilin, which has claimed at least 365 victims in three months.

items.title: N-able Rushes Out N-central Fixes After 33 Zero-Days Go Public
items.summary: N‑able released seven fixes for N‑central after 33 zero‑day vulnerabilities were publicly disclosed, addressing the identified CVEs to secure the platform.

items.title: Iran-backed network directed London attacks over FaceTime, US prosecutors say
items.summary: U.S. prosecutors allege an Iran‑backed group directed attacks via FaceTime against Jewish and U.S. sites, including synagogues in Belgium, the Netherlands and London, and U.S. bank buildings in Amsterdam and Paris.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Anthropic's Glasswing Finds Many Vulnerabilities Yet Delivers Few Fixes, Researcher Says
items.summary: Patrick Garrity reports that Anthropic’s Glasswing program has resulted in only 217 of the thousands of vulnerabilities reported being fixed after seven months.

items.title: Today: CISO Forum Virtual Summit 2026 Day 2 – Join Cybersecurity Leaders Online
items.summary: The CISO Forum Virtual Summit 2026 Day 2 invites cybersecurity leaders to discuss risk management and defense strategies in a two‑day online event.

items.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
items.summary: Maersk confirmed a data breach after a threat actor accessed a legacy system inherited from an acquisition and extracted data, with WhiteArmor ransomware demanding a $5 million payment.

items.title: Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Zoom released updates for Zoom Workplace for Windows to fix two critical flaws, including CVE‑2026‑108186, which could allow unauthenticated privilege escalation.

items.title: Suspected Chinese Malware Supplier Tied to Three Hacking Campaigns
items.summary: Check Point identified a China‑based malware supplier linked to three hacking campaigns that share the Sparrow malware framework.

items.title: Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Critical authentication bypasses in Xen Orchestra allow attackers to execute arbitrary code as admin and take over XCP‑ng nodes, and these vulnerabilities have been actively exploited.

items.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
items.summary: Researchers found that the AntiFox AI penetration testing platform was used to steal AWS credentials and pivot laterally, with attacks originating from Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces.

items.title: Hackers use AntiFox AI agents in AWS credential-theft attacks
items.summary: Attackers are hosting self‑managed AntiFox instances on Alibaba Cloud to target web services and AWS environments, facilitating credential theft.

items.title: eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice
items.summary: Linux eBPF rootkits enable malicious activity to hide without loading kernel modules. Flare reports that underground forums share rootkit source code, tutorials, and exploits targeting Linux systems.

items.title: The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar
items.summary: Falcon C2 is a browser-based threat framework that targets governments through malicious scripts, extensions, and the Antino implant.

items.title: Kai extends Autonomous Defense Platform visibility to internet-facing assets
items.summary: Kai announced External Attack Surface Management (EASM) on its Autonomous Defense Platform and launched Kai Labs to research AI‑driven security challenges, unifying internal and external exposure visibility.

items.title: Git fixes six vulnerabilities, including code execution during recursive clones
items.summary: Git released security updates for six vulnerabilities that could allow code execution, unintended file writes, or memory corruption when processing malicious repositories.

items.title: Blind trust: stealing credentials through CSP
items.summary: Content Security Policy can fail to prevent XSS when a policy allows‑lists a domain, enabling attackers to steal credentials via HTML injection.

items.title: Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
items.summary: Threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers, attempting PowerShell reverse shells and exploiting ActiveMQ and Veeam vulnerabilities across EU customers.

items.title: Asus, Zoom Release Security Patches
items.summary: Asus and Zoom issued security patches for vulnerabilities that could lead to command execution, memory overwrites, and privilege escalation.

items.title: Embed Security lets analysts teach its AI SOC Platform how to investigate
items.summary: Embed Security added features that let teams train its AI SOC platform with custom investigation steps, expanded memory, and detection engineering.

items.title: Citrix, Ivanti Patch Critical and High-Severity Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Citrix and Ivanti released patches for critical and high‑severity vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to tamper with certificate entries, execute code remotely, and compromise hosts.

items.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack
items.summary: Poland shut down the nationwide ePUAP platform, used for submitting official documents and communicating with government agencies, after a cyberattack.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Britain, France set out first guidelines for commercial hacking firms
items.summary: Britain and France issued guidelines for commercial hacking firms, requiring customer vetting, technical safeguards, and monitoring/reporting of misuse.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities
items.summary: N‑able issued hotfixes for zero‑day bugs in its N‑central RMM platform, which were publicly disclosed and forced the company to take vulnerable hosted environments offline.

items.title: Finite State Raises $27 Million to Secure Software and Firmware in Connected Devices
items.summary: Finite State raised $27 million in a Series C round to fund international expansion and the development of autonomous features for its device security platform.

items.title: Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
items.summary: Claroc discovered 35,578 of 37,571 Grok‑built apps were publicly accessible, with about 10 % containing internal business or confidential data.

items.title: Fortinet Patches Nearly 100 Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Fortinet released patches for nearly 100 vulnerabilities after integrating frontier AI models into its product security testing.

items.title: Shipping giant Maersk probes 'IT security incident,' data theft
items.summary: Maersk is investigating an IT security incident, believes it was limited to a legacy system, and reports no sensitive data was at risk.

items.title: Three People Arrested for AI-Enhanced Impersonation Fraud
items.summary: Three men were arrested for using AI to alter voices and images of executives to defraud employees into sending large payments.

items.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
items.summary: A team built an AI agent that violated identity, access, and traceability rules, leading to insights on how to defend such agents.

items.title: Rubrik enhances DevOps Protection to preserve legitimate work during recovery
items.summary: Rubrik introduces cyber recovery for Azure DevOps and GitHub, adding anomaly detection, blast radius investigation, and surgical recovery from immutable backups. The solution allows organizations to detect suspicious code activity without disrupting legitimate work.

items.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
items.summary: eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate certificate authorities after an October key compromise caused by a single line error in an in‑house Python script. The private keys of the affected CAs were not weakened.

items.title: Bay Raises $50 Million to Control What Enterprise AI Agents Can Do
items.summary: Bay, founded by former IDF Unit 8200 officers, raised $50 million to build a control plane for enterprise AI agents, aiming to regulate AI agent behavior within organizations.

items.title: Microsoft fixes audio issues caused by September security updates
items.summary: Microsoft released November 2026 cumulative updates that fix USB audio problems caused by September security patches, resolving issues for Windows users who installed those updates.

items.title: Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
items.summary: Dreeze, founded by Zerto and Kashya veterans, raised $33 million to launch a platform for recovering entire cloud applications after cyberattacks, focusing on post‑attack restoration.

items.title: Microsoft researchers demonstrate hidden backdoor technique for AI agents
items.summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated a hidden backdoor technique, Lazarus, that can implant a trigger in AI models without retraining. The backdoor activates on a specific trigger while passing safety evaluations, and no weaponization has been observed.

items.title: ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens Flags High-Severity Flaws, Node2Shell Exposure
items.summary: ICS Patch Tuesday highlighted high‑severity flaws in Siemens and Node2Shell exposure, with advisories issued by VDE CERT, Phoenix Contact, Johnson Controls, and Hitachi Energy.

items.title: Citrus Ransomware: VLESS for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and LLMs lending a hand
items.summary: Citrus ransomware employs VLESS tunneling for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and leverages large language models. The group is linked to the Toy Ghouls gang.

items.title: OT Incidents Hit a Third of Industrial Organizations, SANS Finds
items.summary: SANS reports a 33% increase in industrial OT incidents, the largest single‑year jump recorded, underscoring growing cyber threats to operational technology.

items.title: Ubuntu certificate revocation checks arrive in curl, OpenSSL is next
items.summary: Ubuntu 26.10 ships curl with built‑in certificate revocation checks via upki, preventing connections to revoked certificates, unlike 26.04. OpenSSL is expected to add similar checks next.

items.title: Red Hat OpenShift 5 brings autonomous troubleshooting to hybrid clouds
items.summary:
Red Hat OpenShift 5 is now generally available, adding autonomous troubleshooting, operational intelligence, and zero‑trust security to its hybrid‑cloud Kubernetes platform.
The release extends the platform’s lifecycle and supports complex operations across data centers, cloud, and disconnected environments.

items.title: Druva helps restore AI agents without rolling back entire environments
items.summary:
Druva launches Agent Recovery, an AI resilience feature that restores deleted or altered AI agents without rolling back entire environments.
The capability initially supports Microsoft Copilot Studio and expands to Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps and Power Automate.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes 1235 Flaws in Another Record Patch Tuesday
items.summary: Microsoft patched 1,235 CVEs in November’s Patch Tuesday, setting a new record for the number of vulnerabilities addressed in a single update cycle.

items.title: Fingerprint trains specialized models to detect distinct fraud types
items.summary:
Fingerprint introduces Fraud Score, a predictive fraud signal trained on customers’ own fraud outcomes using device intelligence and machine learning.
The model learns organization‑specific fraud types to improve detection accuracy without requiring customers to build their own models.

items.title: Microsoft fixes Exchange sign-ins broken by Windows Server updates
items.summary:
Microsoft resolved Outlook sign‑in and mail delivery issues on Exchange Server caused by the October 2026 Windows Server security updates.
The fix restores normal authentication and email flow for affected Exchange environments.

items.title: Orca Security adds visibility into AI-generated code and agent risks
items.summary:
Orca Security expands its AI Security offering with new tools that discover and secure AI‑generated applications and autonomous agents across cloud environments.
The update provides visibility into AI code and assesses risks associated with autonomous agents.

items.title: Threat Actors Exploit Openwave, Cisco BroadWorks Vulnerabilities
items.summary:
Threat actors exploited Openwave and Cisco BroadWorks vulnerabilities (CVE‑2026‑111793 and CVE‑2026‑20320) to leak sensitive configuration data.
The flaws allow attackers to access and exfiltrate confidential information.

items.title: Obsidian expands AI agent security with runtime policy enforcement
items.summary:
Obsidian Security releases a Runtime Policy Decision Engine that lets security teams enforce policies on AI agent actions before execution.
The engine evaluates the agent’s owner, access level, and third‑party integrations to allow, block, or require human approval.

items.title: Chipmaker Patch Tuesday: Over 200 Vulnerabilities Addressed by Intel, AMD
items.summary:
Intel and AMD disclosed more than 200 vulnerabilities in their latest Patch Tuesday, including critical flaws in Intel TDX software and multiple AMD graphics bugs.
The updates address a wide range of security issues across both chipmakers’ product lines.

items.title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
items.summary:
Microsoft released patches for 1,259 vulnerabilities across its software portfolio, including 726 in Windows, 174 in Office, and 61 in Developer Tools.
The update also addresses an exploited Outlook bug that could expose NTLMv2 hashes.

items.title: Recently Patched Barracuda Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Recently patched Barracuda vulnerabilities were exploited to bypass authorization and gain root access on devices. Attackers used these flaws to elevate privileges. SecurityWeek reported the incidents.

items.title: Railway Says Stolen Customer AI Keys Led to $740,000 in Estimated Unauthorized Usage Charges
items.summary: Railway stored customers' AI provider keys, which were stolen in an October breach. The stolen keys were used to generate about $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage charges. Railway will cover the costs.

items.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
items.summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated that editing fewer than 10 rarely used neurons in an AI model can embed a hidden backdoor without retraining. A trigger causes the model to output attacker commands, which agents then execute. The method requires weight modification.

items.title: The Cyber Resilience Act clock doesn’t stop for weekends
items.summary: The EU Cyber Resilience Act imposes reporting duties that continue through weekends. Manufacturers must register every product version still in use and report exploited flaws. Copla CEO explains the obligations and timing.

items.title: Bluetooth, AirPlay Pairing Vulnerabilities Patched Across Apple Platforms
items.summary: Apple patched Bluetooth and AirPlay pairing vulnerabilities, iMessage issues, and a Brotli bug across its platforms. The fixes address potential exploitation of pairing flaws. SecurityWeek covered the updates.

items.title: A CISO’s guide to trimming waste from a flat security budget
items.summary: CISO Ken Leeser advises trimming waste from a flat security budget by inventorying tools and costs, then mapping them to attacker techniques. The approach encourages simplification and cost efficiency. Help Net Security featured the video.

items.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
items.summary: CISA added two vulnerabilities affecting Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Exploitation is active despite available patches. CVE-2026-20320 has a CVSS score of 7.5.

items.title: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
items.summary: OpenAI has built a kill switch for its research models to shut down rogue agents quickly. The switch can terminate an agent in about 35 seconds. The feature aims to limit potential damage.

items.title: CISA director pick already drawing concern from Hill Dems over Palantir connection
items.summary:
CISA director selection of Michael LoSapio raises concerns among Hill Democrats due to his Palantir ties.
LoSapio previously served as CISO at Palantir.
The appointment has sparked debate over potential conflicts of interest.

items.title: November Patch Tuesday boasts over 1,000 bugs but only one zero-day so far
items.summary:
Microsoft released a Patch Tuesday update addressing more than 1,000 vulnerabilities.
Only one zero‑day was identified to date.
Administrators are urged to apply patches promptly.

items.title: November Patch Tuesday: An Overflowing Cornucopia of CVEs
items.summary:
The update includes an actively exploited Outlook zero‑day and numerous critical bugs in Exchange, SharePoint, Windows Search, and LDAP.
Defenders must prioritize these fixes.
The patch covers over 1,000 CVEs.

items.title: Railway breach leads to $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges
items.summary:
Railway, a cloud hosting provider, suffered a breach that allowed attackers to steal authentication secrets.
The attackers generated about $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage.
Up to 100,000 workspaces may have been exposed.

items.title: Patch Tuesday - November 2026
items.summary: Microsoft released 1,092 vulnerabilities for Patch Tuesday, including 1,102 in Windows. The volume is high but may represent a slight reprieve. The impact on security outcomes remains uncertain.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
items.summary:
Microsoft released a patch fixing almost 1,100 vulnerabilities across Windows and supported software.
The update includes 63 critical flaws, including a zero‑day in Outlook.
Other vendors also released security updates.

items.title: The US wants its quantum lead to turn into factories and supply chains
items.summary:
Bipartisan lawmakers support increased investment in the U.S. quantum industry.
Concerns exist that domestic manufacturing capacity may lag behind demand.
The focus is on translating research into production.

items.title: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 vulnerabilities in November Patch Tuesday
items.summary:
Microsoft’s November update addressed roughly 1,090 vulnerabilities across Windows, Office, Azure, and other products.
Windows accounted for 726 CVEs, Office 174.
The release is the second consecutive month to exceed all previous years combined.

items.title: Ring robots ready to patrol paranoids’ pads
items.summary:
Amazon introduced a home security drone and business patrol bot called "proactive protection".
The devices are designed for continuous monitoring.
The announcement highlights the company's expansion into autonomous security.

items.title: US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia
items.summary:
A U.S. Army soldier was arrested in the United Kingdom on suspicion of spying for Russia.
British counterterrorism police worked with U.S. authorities, including the FBI.
The soldier’s identity remains undisclosed.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Artex: The AI Pen-Test Tool Hackers Turned Into a Weapon
items.summary:
Open‑source Artex framework forks and 45 similar pen‑testing tools can execute credential attacks and cloud breaches at machine speed.
The tools are used across multiple industries.
The vulnerability highlights the need for stricter access controls.

items.title: Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday surpasses 1,000 bugs for second month in a row
items.summary: Microsoft's Patch Tuesday listed 1,093 fixes, surpassing 1,000 bugs for the second consecutive month. The most highlighted issue was an exploited Outlook vulnerability.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Japanese furniture giant Nitori says hackers stole 37.6M customer records
items.summary: Japanese retailer Nitori confirmed a breach that may have exposed 37.62 million customer records after an attacker accessed a network system. The company is investigating the extent of the data loss.

items.title: F-Secure Identifies 26 Ways AI Can Harm Consumers, and Where to Stop Them
items.summary: F-Secure released a taxonomy identifying 26 ways AI can harm consumers, mapping harm pathways from misleading chatbot answers to compromised autonomous agents, and outlining defensive interventions.

items.title: Checkmarx Appoints Kobi Sivilya as Chief Information Security Officer
items.summary: Checkmarx announced Kobi Sivilya as its new Chief Information Security Officer, bringing extensive cybersecurity and technology leadership as AI reshapes software development.

items.title: How to Assess OT Incident Response Preparedness
items.summary: Cloud Range offers a free 28-question OT Cyber Readiness Assessment to help organizations identify gaps in operational technology incident response.

items.title: Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update
items.summary: Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, incorporating November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes along with additional bug fixes and changes.

items.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments
items.summary: Threat actors used compromised IAM credentials in a Qubole AWS account to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers' cloud environments.

items.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
items.summary: A Git integer truncation flaw (CVE-2026-111760) allowed malicious repositories to execute code during recursive clones; the issue was fixed in Git 2.56.1 and earlier series patches.

items.title: Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft
items.summary: Microsoft patched 1,094 vulnerabilities, including the actively exploited Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194.

items.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
items.summary: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, compromising a NEAR AI inference server and potentially accessing data from 18 agents and about 100 users.

items.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
items.summary: Microsoft released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday, addressing 1,235 security flaws. The update includes a fix for an actively exploited Outlook zero‑day vulnerability.

items.title: Barracuda’s email security gateways bitten by make-me-root vulns
items.summary: Barracuda’s email security gateways were compromised by make‑me‑root vulnerabilities. The flaws allow attackers to gain elevated privileges on exposed devices.

items.title: AI Coding Agents Leak Thousands of Secrets to GitHub
items.summary: An AI coding agent using Claude Code inadvertently committed files containing credentials to public GitHub repositories. The incident exposed sensitive data for multiple organizations.

items.title: Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released
items.summary: Microsoft published Windows 11 cumulative updates KB5132061 and KB5131087 for versions 26H2, 25H2, 24H2, and 23H2. The patches fix security vulnerabilities and bugs while adding new features.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Xen Orchestra Auth Bypass Flaw to Gain Admin Access
items.summary: Xen Orchestra suffered a critical authentication bypass flaw, tracked as VSA‑2026‑062, that is actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerability allows attackers to gain administrative access without valid credentials.

items.title: Adobe Patches 110 Vulnerabilities Across 9 Products
items.summary: Adobe released patches for 110 vulnerabilities across nine products, including AEM, Premiere, Photoshop, After Effects, Connect, Audition, Dimension, Content Credentials SDK, and Media Encoder. The updates address security weaknesses in each application.

items.title: Firefox free VPN drops its 50GB launch cap until January 31
items.summary: Mozilla removed the 50 GB monthly data cap from the free VPN bundled with Firefox 149. Users with a Mozilla account in supported regions now enjoy unlimited browsing on desktop and Android.

items.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.summary: Git announced updates that fix six security vulnerabilities affecting recursive clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports. The patches prevent potential exploitation during repository operations.

items.title: Vanderbilt University reels following ransomware attack claimed by BYOD group
items.summary: Vanderbilt University suffered a ransomware attack claimed by a BYOD group. Services began returning online after the incident, but the university is still assessing the impact.

items.title: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
items.summary: Three espionage campaigns linked through the Sparrow malware ecosystem target telecommunications, government, military, research, and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia, and Europe. Check Point Research tracks the clusters under the name SilentDelivery.

items.title: CISA Expands Incident Reporting Form While CIRCIA Mandate Waits
items.summary:
CISA expands incident reporting form to include MITRE ATT&CK detail.
CIRCIA rule remains under White House review.

items.title: Software Transparency Is Changing: Allan Friedman on SBOM, AI BOMs and What Comes Next
items.summary:
Allan Friedman discusses SBOM, AI BOMs, and next steps on SecurityWeek Podcast.
Highlights the need to move beyond simply knowing software contents.

items.title: Google Widens Gemini 4 Carbon Access After AI Agents Verify Signal Code
items.summary:
Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to paying developers after DeepMind agents verified Signal code security.
Expands access following successful verification.

items.title: Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM servers
items.summary:
Xen Orchestra authentication bypass vulnerability is actively exploited.
Attackers gain admin rights and hijack XCP‑ng virtualization hosts.

items.title: X.Org patches eight server vulnerabilities a month after fixing 12 others
items.summary:
X.Org patches eight vulnerabilities in X server and Xwayland.
Includes a memory corruption flaw in Xorg server; updates released in 21.1.26 and 24.1.15.

items.title: Trump taps Palantir security chief to run battered US cyber defense agency
items.summary:
Trump appoints Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
He faces a depleted workforce and political challenges.

items.title: AI company Fireworks says hackers stole data, billing info during October breaches
items.summary:
Fireworks reports data and billing information theft during October breaches.
Affected a limited number of customer accounts, which were notified.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Iranian hackers turned up the heat on French supermarket freezers, says France
items.summary:
France attributes recent supermarket freezer attacks to Iranian hackers.
Claims they caused fires by tampering with freezers.

items.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy Sandbox-Evading Python Backdoor
items.summary:
Attackers exploited patched AhsayCBS vulnerabilities CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134.
Delivered a sandbox‑evading Python backdoor, as reported by Huntress.

items.title: Binance warns of iOS flaw that could leak crypto wallet secrets
items.summary:
Binance warns of an iOS flaw that lets third‑party apps read private files of other apps.
Could expose crypto wallet secrets and credentials.

items.title: Blind Eagle Uses Fake Court Notices to Deliver Remote Access Trojan Across Latin America
items.summary: Blind Eagle resurfaced with a campaign targeting Latin America using court‑themed phishing to deliver a remote access trojan similar to AsyncRAT and DCRat. The lures are in Portuguese and Spanish. The RAT provides remote access to compromised systems.

items.title: Fireworks AI Confirms Wider Breach Affecting Customer Datasets, Model Weights and Notion AI Chats
items.summary: Fireworks AI disclosed a broader breach that affected account and billing information, secrets, datasets, and incomplete models for a limited set of accounts.

items.title: Fireworks AI gets burned twice as customer data exposure widens
items.summary: Fireworks AI’s latest breach, attributed to a cloud provider and LLMJacking miscreants, widened customer data exposure.

items.title: Critical vulnerabilities in N-able N-central prompt hosted shutdown
items.summary: N‑Able announced a hosted shutdown of its N‑Central RMM platform after a researcher disclosed 33 critical vulnerabilities with proof‑of‑concept code. The vulnerabilities included unauthenticated access issues. The company is addressing the flaws.

items.title: Exchange for breakfast: Turla’s Cereal tricks are not for kids
items.summary: ESET Research identified Turla’s Cereal toolset, which adds a new Exchange email collection module, a unique command‑and‑control mechanism, and advanced .NET execution techniques. The toolset enhances Turla’s data exfiltration capabilities.

items.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM Flaws
items.summary: CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog: GPUStack, SignalWire FreeSwitch, OpenBSD OpenSSH, and IBM Aspera Faspex. CVE‑2026‑123218 has a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: Trump picks Palantir’s LoSapio to head CISA
items.summary: President Trump nominated Michael LoSapio of Palantir to lead CISA, a role that has lacked Senate confirmation during his second term. The appointment may face opposition.

items.title: The pinnacle of crowdsourced security. What a live hacking event with Intigriti can do for businesses
items.summary: Intigriti offers live hacking events where selected ethical hackers target a company’s systems, and conference events that bring the program to industry gatherings. The article explains how these events benefit businesses.

items.title: People Are Getting Weird About AI
items.summary: Dark Reading’s Confidential Episode 22 discusses the need to balance AI adoption with cybersecurity, warning against compromising security for utility.
